# Dataset note

**All data in this folder is synthetic**, generated by `src/generate_dataset.py` with a fixed
seed (42). It is not STEG data and not a measured grid dataset.

## Files

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `simulated_energy_readings.csv` | 3,600 rows: 5 meters (`meter_01` … `meter_05`) on one feeder (`feeder_F1`), hourly, 1–30 January 2026. Columns: timestamp, feeder_id, meter_id, active_power_kw, voltage_v, current_a, label, category, event_id, is_synthetic |
| `injected_events.csv` | One row per injected event: ID, type, category, meters, start, end, duration and generation method |

## How the baseline is generated

- **Power:** a daily household shape (morning bump, evening peak, slightly higher at weekends), scaled per meter for household size, with multiplicative log-normal noise (σ = 0.10).
- **Voltage:** a shared feeder voltage around 230 V that sags slightly when the street is busy, plus a fixed line drop per meter and small noise.
- **Current:** I = P / V plus small noise, so P ≈ V × I holds for normal readings.

## How each anomaly is generated

See the table in the main README or `injected_events.csv`. Eight events affect a single meter
(data-quality problems); two affect all five meters at once (genuine grid events: a voltage
sag and an outage). The `label` column holds the event type, `category` holds
`data_quality`, `grid_event` or `normal`, and `event_id` links each row to its event.

## Real measured baseline (UCI)

Download: <https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/321/electricityloaddiagrams20112014>

`python src/generate_dataset.py --uci <LD2011_2014 file>` replaces the synthetic household
power with real 15-minute consumption from UCI ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014 (370 clients in
Portugal, 2011–2014, kW per 15 minutes, CC BY 4.0), averaged to hourly. Only power is
measured: voltage, current and all injected events remain simulated, so `is_synthetic` is
True for injected rows and `power_source` records where the power came from. Selection rules
for the 5 clients are in `src/load_uci.py`. Outputs: `uci_feeder_readings.csv`,
`uci_injected_events.csv`, `uci_client_selection.csv`.

## Phase 2

STEG open data, if usable, will be used to scale profiles to Tunisian load patterns, and the
UCI Individual Household Electric Power Consumption dataset (real voltage and current) to test
the physics check on measured values.
